title: Use Our Take Home Pay Calc to Compare the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates
description: Convert hourly to annual pay with our take home pay calc. Compare the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, super, and tax for a 38‑hour week.
salarySummary: Based on a 38‑hour week, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, giving an annual gross of about $52,245 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I use the take home pay calc to compare award rates?
faqs.a: Enter your base hourly rate from your award or the National Minimum Wage. The timesheet on the home page multiplies it by hours per week (default 38) and 52 weeks. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. The result shows gross annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. Then the estimate deducts tax and Medicare levy and adds 12% super on top (up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base). This gives you a take‑home pay calc that you can adjust for different award rates.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award. Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries or occupations and are often higher. Awards also include penalty rates, allowances, and classifications. Our take home pay calc uses the base rate you enter; if you have an award rate, enter that instead of the minimum wage. The calc does not automatically apply award‑specific penalties, so you should add those separately if needed.

faqs.q: Does the take home pay calc include casual loading and super?
faqs.a: Yes. On the home page, a checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate you type. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. The tax estimate uses the 2026–27 resident tax scale and the 2% Medicare levy (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). The result is an estimate only—it does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

bodyMarkdown:
## Convert Hourly to Annual Pay with Our Take Home Pay Calc

Whether you are negotiating a salary or checking a job offer, our **take home pay calc** helps you see the full picture. You start with an hourly rate—from the National Minimum Wage, an award, or a casual job—and the calculator shows your gross annual pay, fortnightly pay, weekly pay, estimated tax, and super. This article explains the assumptions behind the numbers and how to compare different pay structures.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

Annual gross pay is simply your hourly rate multiplied by the number of hours you work each week, then multiplied by 52 weeks. For a full‑time employee working 38 hours a week (the standard under the Fair Work Act), the formula is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. That gives:

- Annual gross: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44 (rounded)
- Weekly gross: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72
- Fortnightly gross: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44

Our [timesheet (home page)](/) uses this formula. You can change the hours per week if you work part‑time or a different roster. The calculator assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour.

Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries (e.g., hospitality, retail, manufacturing). They are often higher than the National Minimum Wage and include classifications for different skill levels. For example, a Level 1 retail employee might have a higher base rate than the minimum wage. Our **take home pay calc** lets you enter any base rate, so you can compare your award rate to the minimum. If you are on an award, use the rate from your [pay guides](/blog) or your employer.

**Important:** The calculator does not automatically apply award‑specific penalty rates or allowances. You would need to adjust the hourly rate to include those if they apply to your regular hours.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. On the home page, a checkbox adds this loading. **Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading**—the calculator adds it for you. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour.

For award rates, the casual loading is often 25% as well, but some awards have different loadings. Check your award or agreement. The calculator uses 25% as the default.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Reference

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly gross by 2. Using the minimum wage example:

- Weekly: $1,004.72
- Fortnightly: $2,009.44

Our [reference tables](/data) include fortnightly figures for common hourly rates.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

The **take home pay calc** estimates tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed in this estimate. It assumes you are a resident with the full tax‑free threshold and no dependants.

For the minimum wage example ($52,245 gross), the estimated tax and Medicare would be:

- Tax: $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 = $4,020, then 30% on $7,245 = $2,173.50 → total tax $6,193.50
- Medicare: 2% of $52,245 = $1,044.90
- Total deductions: $7,238.40
- Estimated take‑home pay: $52,245 – $7,238.40 = $45,006.60 per year

This is an estimate. The Australian Taxation Office provides the official rates.

### Super Guarantee: Paid on Top

Superannuation is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It does not come out of your hourly rate. The calculator adds 12% to your annual gross, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27). For the minimum wage example:

- Super: 12% of $52,245 = $6,269.40 (well under the cap)
- Total employer cost: $52,245 + $6,269.40 = $58,514.40

Super is not included in your take‑home pay; it goes into your super fund. Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page explains more.

### Comparing a Salary Offer to an Hourly Rate

If you are offered a salary, you can reverse the calculation. Divide the annual salary by 52 weeks, then by hours per week (usually 38) to get the equivalent hourly rate. Then use our **take home pay calc** to see the after‑tax amount. Remember that salary often includes leave entitlements, while hourly rates may be casual with loading.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more details, see our pages on [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage), [take-home pay](/topics/take-home), [average pay](/topics/average-pay) (which includes ABS averages, not job medians), [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion), [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading), and [job pay](/topics/job-pay).
